entries.title: 3 John 1:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines

entries.title: 3 John 1:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Or, pray.

q This Gaius was well known by the Apostle, not only to be a stedfast Professor of the truly Christian uncorrupted Faith, (which is imply'd in his avowing his Love to him in the Truth, or upon the Christian account) but to be so improv'd, and well-grown a Christian, that he reckons he might well make the prosperous State of his Soul, the measure of all the other Prosperity he could wish unto him.

entries.title: 3 John 1:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines

entries.title: 3 John 1:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
s i. e. Such as had been converted to Christ by his Ministry, (as 1 Cor. 4.15.) of whom it appears Gaius was one, did walk in the Truth; (an apt Expression of such correspondent Practice) was greatest matter of Joy to this holy Apostle, especially when the godly Lives of such, to whose Conversion he had been instrumental, were so observable, as to gain them a Testimony from all others that knew them, as it was in the present Instance.

r The Truth is familiarly used to signifie the pure Doctrine of Christianity, which in its principal Design, aiming at correspondent Practice; that his Children,

entries.title: 3 John 1:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: t Charity to Christians is reckon'd Fidelity to Christ, being shown to them upon the Christian Account, which is intimated to have been done by this pious Person, who so kindly treated the Brethren, and Strangers, i. e. even tho they were Strangers.

entries.title: 3 John 1:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: u i. e. After a manner (as the Greek Expression is) worthy of God, viz. as becomes them, who bear the Name of God, as thou dost, or are intent upon his Work, as they are; which latter notion is confirmed by what follows.

entries.title: 3 John 1:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: x It thence appears these were Iews, who went out from their own Country to serve the Interest of the Gospel, which therefore he should serve in helping them.

entries.title: 3 John 1:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: y This was probably some Church of which Gaius was. Dio[illegible]rephes, one who had received, or usurped some Office or Authority in it, to so ill a purpose, as when he had no Inclination to be hospitable himself to fellow-Christians, prevented others from being so; and upon pretence of the little differences of these Iewish, from the Gentile Christians, excluded them their Communion.

entries.title: 3 John 1:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Psal. 37.27. Isa. 1.16. 1 Pet. 3.11.

z [illegible]: By following here he means Imitation, i. e. the Deformity of evil appearing in the Practice of some, and the Beauty of true Goodness in others, (Examples being given of both sorts, v. 9, and 12.) he exhorts to decline the former, and imitate the other; and enforces the Exhortation by the weightiest Arguments.

a A Doer of good, one made up of Kind[illegible]ess and E[illegible]ignity (as the Context draws the sense to that special kind of Goodness, [illegible] & [illegible], signifie doing well or ill, from a fixed prevailing habit, 1 Iohn 3.7, 8.

b Is ally'd to Heaven, born of God, his Off-spring.

c An evil Doer on the other hand, such a one as is a Composition of Spite, Envy, and Malice, is a meer Stranger to him, hath not been, or known, or had to do with him.

entries.title: 3 John 1:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: d Some eminent Christian, whom he could with confidence recommend as a Pattern.

entries.title: 3 John 1:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: e Having much more to say, as 2 Iohn 12. he resolved on a more immediate, grateful, and effectual way of imparting, and even impressing his Sense, as the term, Writing, is used in a greater latitude, Prov. 3.3. and elsewhere.

entries.title: 3 John 1:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Gr. mouth to mouth.

f [illegible], viz. by oral Conferenc[illegible], which he hoped ere long to have opportunity for. He concludes with the usual Christian Salutations.
